name: Grey White
lede: Grey white is a pale warm off-white, and in our data a paint-industry name from the RAL system.

sections.title: What it names
sections.body:
Our library takes this swatch from RAL 9002, an industrial color standard, so it is an approximate screen value for a paint [1]. Paterson defines grey white only in passing, as chalk's color [2]. Its nearest everyday name is [[ecru]], 6.1 units away, and it sits beside [[ivory]], [[silver]] and [[white]] [1].

The books mostly use the phrase for something else, a moral palette. Pastoureau notes that Protestant reformers' dress codes leaned on dark colors, blacks, greys and browns, with white for children, and that the Reformation favored a split between black, grey and white and the "true" colors [3][4]. He also wonders whether this moral outlook narrowed the colors of early manufactured goods [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In the archive, 994 of 23,781 paintings carry this tone, almost all as highlights: 99 per cent of the matched area sits in the lightest zone [5]. China stands out, with 105 of 635 works, about four times the archive rate, [5]. The data are photographs of aged, varnished works, so a match is approximate [5].
